issue: On 30 Jan 2026 Morocco's Ministry for Energy Transition suspended the tender for the Nador West Med LNG terminal (a separate GEM terminal) and associated pipelines, citing 'new parameters and hypotheses' and signalling a review of the whole 2024-2030 gas roadmap. Dakhla LNG is Phase two (post-2030) of that same roadmap and depends on it; no source yet says Dakhla itself is suspended, advanced, or cancelled, so its 'proposed' status is unchanged for now. The Dakhla Atlantique PORT remains on track for 2028 commissioning, but that is the port, not the LNG component. Flagging because the project's own researcher note (2026-05-05) asked to track whether the rest of the plan is being reconsidered after Nador.
suggested_action: No field edit now (status genuinely still 'proposed'; fetch_timeline endpoint is down regardless). Watch for any official restatement of the gas roadmap that explicitly retains, defers, or drops the Atlantic-coast/Dakhla terminal; if the roadmap is formally cancelled or Dakhla is dropped, route a Status change (proposed -> cancelled/shelved) to a follow-on Update once a primary source confirms. Sources: enerdata.net (30 Jan 2026 suspension), moroccoworldnews.com (Feb 2026, Nador suspension + roadmap context).
